messages:
Incident Bot: ALERT — apigw-edge-prod: 5xx rate spike detected (502/504). 15m error rate 18% (baseline 0.6%). affected region: us-west-2. auto-page sent to #incidents and oncall. :rotating_light:
Sara (oncall): saw it. paging Mike (primary).
Mike R: here — I'm oncall. initial check: dashboards show request fanout spike hitting gateway upstream pools, 502s originate at edge before auth. digging into LB target health.
Jordan H: noticed a small deploy 12m ago to edge-proxy-v2, but nothing obvious in deploy logs. throwing up a quick canary rollback as precaution.
Alesha G: from logs — connection resets and TLS handshake failures to backend pool fqdn-edge-backend-1 around same window. snippet: ```
[2026-03-15T23:09:12Z] upstream error: tls: handshake failure -> reset
[2026-03-15T23:09:14Z] backend 10.20.5.12: upstream returned 502
```
Kevin P: checking infra — no host OOMs, CPU ok. but target group health shows growing 5xx health checks on port 8443. could be cert rotation?
Mike R: good call. rolling edge-proxy-v2 -> initiating quick rollback to v1 (canary). command: `k rollout restart deployment/edge-proxy -n prod --selector=version=v1-canary` will route ~10% to v1 immediately.
Support CS: getting customer alerts — CS reporting API errors for some customers, ticket #INC-9082. Can we estimate impacted requests/min and map to customers?
Sara (oncall): estimate ~8% of total traffic impacted in us-west-2, top affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/stream. send customer list to Support CS after we confirm mitigation.
Jordan H: I've flipped the canary. traffic routing shows fall from 18% -> 9% 3 minutes after; still noisy.
Alesha G: correlation: an automated cert renew job ran 20m ago for internal mTLS certs on fqdn-edge-backend-1. I'm rolling back that change with infra team to test.
Mike R: also enabling circuit-breaker on apigw route to reduce fanout to backend pools: `route config set --circuit-breaker apigw --max-concurrent 150 --pending-request-samples 20` — should give quick relief.
Incident Bot: NOTE — auto-scaling disabled during emergency by Mike R (reason: avoid new nodes pulling bad certs).
Kevin P: infra confirms we reverted the cert change on fqdn-edge-backend-1 and restarted backend at 23:12Z. health checks recovered for 3 of 4 hosts. last host stuck in UNHEALTHY -> investigating network path.
Mike R: temporary mitigations in place: rollback canary v1, circuit breaker enabled, backend cert revert. 502 rate down to ~4.5% now. still monitoring.
Support CS: relayed interim message to customers: "We are experiencing elevated API errors in us-west-2; mitigation in progress." requests 12:20 PST. customers asking for ETA.
Sara (oncall): ETA: monitoring for 30m post-stabilization before declaring service restored. assign Jordan and Kevin to continue investigation. Mike to coordinate postmortem.
Jordan H: digging into network path to the one remaining unhealthy host — I see intermittent TLS handshake timeouts to 10.20.5.18 specifically, looks like SNI mismatch after revert. working with infra to restart the sidecar on that host.
Alesha G: when that host recovers, we should run a golden traffic pass and verify end-to-end for /v1/generate and streaming endpoints.
Mike R: agreed. also opening a mitigation-only runbook entry: actions taken, timestamps, commands used, and customer impact estimates. I'll link in the postmortem.
Support CS: customers updated — one enterprise customer with higher error footprint asked for log bundle; queued under legal-approved scrub.
Sara (oncall): handoff plan: if still stable at 23:42Z, handoff to Night Oncall (Kevin) with notes: mitigations, remaining unhealthy host, CS tickets, rollback IDs. I'll draft the handoff summary.
Kevin P: I'll take it, standby for alert re-escalation. add me to INC-9082.
Incident Bot: RESOLVE CHECK — error rate improved to 2.1% (10m average) but not yet normal. follow-up postmortem required.
Mike R: recorded a short runbook entry and pinned commands in thread. will create postmortem ticket and assign to infra + edge teams.
Sara (oncall): good work everyone. final note: don't close CS tickets until we confirm full health for all hosts. I'll post final update after 30m verify. :thumbsup:
